summary: A Kohen who is tamei or who did not have a bris may not eat terumah, but his wife and slaves may. A Kohen with a certain injury may eat terumah, but his wife may not, unless the injury came after they were together as husband and wife.

chunks.en: An uncircumcised Kohen and all who are tamei
chunks.st: An uncircumcised priest, e.g., one for whom circumcision was considered too dangerous, and all those who are ritually impure with any type of impurity,

words.note: A Kohen who could not have a bris because it was dangerous.

chunks.en: may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: may not partake of teruma, the portion of produce that must be set aside for the priests. However,

chunks.en: Their wives and their slaves
chunks.st: their wives and their slaves

chunks.en: may eat terumah.
chunks.st: may partake of teruma. With regard to both

chunks.en: A man with a certain injury, or another kind of such injury,
chunks.explain: Injuries that keep a man from having children.
chunks.st: a man with crushed testicles or with other wounds to his genitals [petzua dakka] and one whose penis has been severed [kerut shofkha], it is prohibited for them to marry a woman who was born Jewish. If they are priests

chunks.en: they and their slaves may eat,
chunks.st: they and their slaves may partake of teruma, as this condition does not disqualify them or their property. However,

chunks.en: but their wives may not eat.
chunks.st: their wives may not partake of teruma, because if a priest has relations with his wife after suffering his injury, he renders her a ḥalala, a woman who is disqualified from marrying a priest, as he has engaged in forbidden sexual relations with her. If such a priest

chunks.en: And if he was not with her as a husband since he became
chunks.st: did not know his wife, i.e., did not engage in sexual relations with her,

chunks.en: injured in this way,
chunks.st: after his testicles were crushed or his penis was severed,

chunks.en: she may eat.
chunks.st: she may partake of teruma, as she had married the priest in a permitted manner.

summary: This mishnah explains which injuries count for the last mishnah. Such a man may not marry a girl born Jewish, but he may marry a convert or a freed maidservant.

chunks.en: Who counts as "injured" (petzua daka)?
chunks.st: And who is deemed a man with crushed testicles? It is

chunks.en: Anyone whose body was injured there,
chunks.st: anyone whose testicles have been wounded,

chunks.en: even only one of them.
chunks.st: even one of them.

chunks.en: And who counts as "cut" (kerus shafchah)?
chunks.st: And one whose penis has been severed is

chunks.en: Anyone whose body part was cut off.
chunks.st: anyone whose sexual member has been cut off. As for the measure that renders him unfit,

chunks.he: וְאִם נִשְׁתַּיֵּר מֵהָעֲטָרָה אֲפִלּוּ כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה,
chunks.en: And if even a hair's width is left of it,
chunks.st: if there remains a portion of the corona, even as much as a hairsbreadth, he is still

chunks.en: he is fit. Petzua daka and kerus shafchah
chunks.st: fit. However, if nothing at all is left of the corona, he is considered as one with a severed penis, for whom it is prohibited by Torah law to marry a Jewish woman. A man with crushed testicles or with other wounds to his genitals and one whose penis has been severed

chunks.en: may marry a convert or a freed maidservant.
chunks.st: are permitted to marry a female convert or an emancipated maidservant,

chunks.en: They are only forbidden to marry into the Jewish people,
chunks.st: and they are prohibited only from entering into the congregation and marrying a woman who was born Jewish,

chunks.en: as it says (Devarim 23),
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: "A man with these injuries
chunks.st: A man wounded with crushed testicles

chunks.en: shall not come into the congregation of Hashem."
chunks.st: or a severed penis shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord” (Deuteronomy 23:2).

summary: Converts from Amon and Moav may never marry girls born Jewish, but their women are allowed right away. Converts from Mitzrayim and Edom must wait three generations. Mamzerim and Nesinim are forbidden forever.

chunks.en: An Amoni and a Moavi
chunks.st: Ammonite and Moabite converts

chunks.en: are forbidden, and forever,
chunks.explain: They may not marry a girl born Jewish.
chunks.st: are prohibited from entering into the congregation and marrying a woman who was born Jewish, and their prohibition is eternal, for all generations.

chunks.en: but their women are allowed right away.
chunks.st: However, their female counterparts, even the convert herself, are permitted immediately.

chunks.en: A Mitzri and an Edomi are forbidden
chunks.st: Egyptian and Edomite converts are prohibited from entering into the congregation

chunks.en: only for three generations,
chunks.st: only for three generations,

chunks.en: both men and women.
chunks.st: both males and females.

chunks.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר אֶת הַנְּקֵבוֹת מִיָּד.
chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon allows the women right away.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon renders permitted Egyptian and Edomite females immediately.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: "This is a kal vachomer:
chunks.st: The matter may be derived by way of an a fortiori inference:

words.note: If something is true in an easy case, it is surely true in a harder one.

chunks.en: If where the Torah forbade
chunks.st: If in a place where the Torah rendered prohibited

chunks.en: the men forever,
chunks.st: the males with an eternal prohibition, i.e., Ammonites and Moabites, it

chunks.en: it allowed the women right away,
chunks.st: rendered permitted the females immediately, then in

chunks.en: then where it forbade the men
chunks.st: a place where it rendered prohibited the males

chunks.en: only for three generations,
chunks.st: for only three generations, i.e., Egyptians and Edomites,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁנַּתִּיר אֶת הַנְּקֵבוֹת מִיָּד.
chunks.en: surely we should allow the women right away!"
chunks.st: is it not right that we should render permitted the females immediately?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon’s colleagues said to him:

chunks.en: "If it is a halachah you learned, we will accept it.
chunks.st: If you are reporting a halakha that you received from your teachers, we will accept it from you.

chunks.en: But if it is your own reasoning,
chunks.st: But if you merely wish to prove your case with an a fortiori inference based on your own reasoning,

chunks.en: there is an answer against it."
chunks.st: there is a refutation of your argument.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: "Not so,
chunks.st: That is not so. I disagree with your claim that the a fortiori inference can be refuted, but in any case

chunks.en: I am saying a halachah."
chunks.st: I am stating a halakha handed down to me by my teachers.

chunks.en: Mamzerim and Nesinim
chunks.st: Mamzerim and the Gibeonites who converted to Judaism in the days of Joshua

chunks.en: are forbidden, and forever,
chunks.st: are prohibited from entering into the congregation and marrying a woman who was born Jewish. Their prohibition is eternal, for all generations, and it applies to

chunks.en: both men
chunks.st: both males

chunks.en: and women.
chunks.st: and females.

summary: Rabbi Yehoshua heard two rulings about a man who cannot have children, one saying he does chalitzah and one saying he does not. Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Eliezer explain them in opposite ways.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: "I heard that a saris does chalitzah,
chunks.st: I heard two rulings from my teachers. One ruling is that a eunuch performs ḥalitza with his yevama,

words.note: A man who cannot have children.

chunks.en: and they do chalitzah with his wife,
chunks.st: and his brothers perform ḥalitza with his wife,

chunks.he: וְהַסָּרִיס לֹא חוֹלֵץ וְלֹא חוֹלְצִין לְאִשְׁתּוֹ,
chunks.en: and that a saris does not do chalitzah, and they do not do chalitzah with his wife,
chunks.st: and the other ruling is that a eunuch does not perform ḥalitza with his yevama, and his brothers do not perform ḥalitza with his wife.

chunks.en: and I cannot explain it."
chunks.st: And I cannot explain these two rulings, as I do not remember the circumstances to which each ruling applies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: "I will explain.
chunks.st: I will explain.

chunks.en: A saris made by people does chalitzah, and they do chalitzah with his wife,
chunks.explain: He was hurt after he was born.
chunks.st: A eunuch caused by man, i.e., one who became emasculated after birth, performs ḥalitza with his yevama and his brothers perform ḥalitza with his wife,

chunks.en: because he had a time when he was fit.
chunks.st: because he had an hour of fitness, a time when he was fertile. On the other hand,

chunks.en: A saris from birth does not do chalitzah
chunks.st: a eunuch by natural causes, i.e., who was entirely lacking in sexual capacity from birth, does not perform ḥalitza with his yevama

chunks.en: and they do not do chalitzah with his wife,
chunks.st: and his brothers do not perform ḥalitza with his wife,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכֹּשֶׁר.
chunks.en: because he never had a time when he was fit."
chunks.st: because he did not have an hour of fitness, as he never had the potential to father children.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: "Not so.
chunks.st: No; rather, the opposite is the case:

chunks.en: Rather, a saris from birth does chalitzah,
chunks.st: A eunuch by natural causes performs ḥalitza with his yevama

chunks.en: and they do chalitzah with his wife,
chunks.st: and his brothers perform ḥalitza with his wife

chunks.en: because he can be healed.
chunks.st: because he can be cured,

chunks.en: A saris made by people does not do chalitzah
chunks.st: whereas a eunuch caused by man does not perform ḥalitza with his yevama

chunks.en: and they do not do chalitzah with his wife,
chunks.st: and his brothers do not perform ḥalitza with his wife

chunks.en: because he cannot be healed."
chunks.st: because he cannot be cured.

chunks.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן בְּתֵירָא עַל
chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beseira told about
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira testified about

chunks.he: בֶּן מְגוּסַת שֶׁהָיָה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם סְרִיס אָדָם,
chunks.en: ben Megusas in Yerushalayim, a saris made by people,
chunks.st: a man named ben Megusat, who lived in Jerusalem and was a eunuch caused by man, that his brothers nevertheless

chunks.en: that they did yibum with his wife,
chunks.st: entered into levirate marriage with his wife, in order

chunks.en: which supports what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: to fulfill and confirm the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

summary: A man or woman who cannot have children does not do yibum or chalitzah. If they did chalitzah anyway, it does not make her unfit, but marrying her does.

chunks.en: A saris does not do chalitzah or yibum.
chunks.st: A sexually underdeveloped man does not perform ḥalitza or enter into levirate marriage with his yevama.

chunks.he: וְכֵן אַיְלוֹנִית לֹא חוֹלֶצֶת וְלֹא מִתְיַבֶּמֶת.
chunks.en: And so an aylonis does not do chalitzah or yibum.
chunks.st: And similarly, a sexually underdeveloped woman [aylonit], who is incapable of bearing children, does not perform ḥalitza or enter into levirate marriage with her yavam.

chunks.en: A saris who did chalitzah with his yevamah
chunks.st: If a sexually underdeveloped man performed ḥalitza with his yevama,

chunks.en: did not make her unfit.
chunks.st: he has not thereby disqualified her from marrying into the priesthood, as his ḥalitza is invalid. However, if

chunks.en: If he married her, he made her unfit,
chunks.st: he had intercourse with her, he has disqualified her. This is

chunks.en: because it was a forbidden marriage.
chunks.st: because it is considered licentious sexual intercourse, since such intercourse does not fulfill the mitzva of levirate marriage and is therefore categorized as forbidden relations with one’s sister-in-law.

chunks.en: And so an aylonis who did chalitzah with the brothers
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to a sexually underdeveloped woman, if one of

chunks.en: was not made unfit.
chunks.st: the brothers performed ḥalitza with her he has not thereby disqualified her from marrying into the priesthood. However, if he

chunks.en: If they married her, they made her unfit,
chunks.st: had intercourse with her, he

chunks.en: because it was a forbidden marriage.
chunks.st: has disqualified her because the intercourse is considered licentious sexual intercourse.

summary: Some unusual cases: a Kohen who cannot have children, or an androginos Kohen, may let his wife eat terumah. The mishnah also discusses a tumtum and an androginos.

chunks.he: סְרִיס חַמָּה כֹּהֵן שֶׁנָּשָׂא בַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: A Kohen who was a saris from birth and married a Jewish woman
chunks.st: If a priest who is a eunuch by natural causes married an Israelite woman, he

chunks.en: lets her eat terumah.
chunks.st: enables her to eat teruma.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say: If

chunks.en: an androginos Kohen who married a Jewish woman
chunks.st: a priest who is a hermaphrodite, possessing both male and female genitals, married an Israelite woman, he

words.note: Someone with signs of both a man and a woman.

chunks.en: lets her eat terumah.
chunks.st: enables her to eat teruma.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: If

chunks.en: a tumtum who was opened and found to be a male
chunks.st: a tumtum, whose external sexual organs are indeterminate, was torn open so that his genitals were exposed, and he was found to be a male, he

words.note: Someone whose body does not show if he is a boy or a girl.

chunks.en: may not do chalitzah,
chunks.st: must not perform ḥalitza,

chunks.en: because he is like a saris.
chunks.st: because he is treated like a eunuch.

chunks.en: An androginos may marry a woman,
chunks.st: A hermaphrodite may marry a woman

chunks.en: but may not be married to a man.
chunks.st: but he may not be married by a man, as he is considered a man.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: If one had intercourse with

chunks.en: an androginos counts like a male, and sinning with him is punished with stoning.
chunks.st: a hermaphrodite, he is liable to receive the punishment of stoning on his account as if he had had relations with a male.
